txt_and_docx_files.text_snippet: Mapping the Collapse of Oyo and the trans-Atlantic Slave Trade, 1816-1836 Henry B. Lovejoy, University of Colorado Boulder Abstract This historical GIS experiment combines geo-political data related to the collapse of the kingdom of Oyo with the departure of slave ships from the Bight of Benin to illustrate migrations of enslaved people through a series of annual maps. This article examines both the achievements and drawbacks of mapping Africa’s uncertain past. An exploration of the sources and methods used to generate data surrounding the dissolution and formation of places during intra-African conflict apropos of the suppression of the Atlantic slave trade makes it possible to represent the likely origins of enslaved people primarily transported to Brazil, Cuba and Sierra Leone between 1
